Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-09-04 | AMZN | Overweight | -1.9% | -0.7% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is Overweight, but built in stages and capped at 1.0x standard allocation until the Q3 print confirms the capex and depreciation trajectory. Stage 1: ~0.30x at 252.00–254.50 (lower band / 9-1 low / just above the rising 50-SMA at 253.95), sized off a realistic stress stop near 248.00 rather than the idealized 2.74-point gap to the 250.76 daily-close invalidation. Stage 2: ~0.30x only on a daily close above 262.20 on ≥40M shares with a next-session hold above 259.78–262.20; Stage 3: ~0.20x only after a confirmed break-and-retest above 267.56 alongside capex or AWS segment confirmation. Do not add at 267.75 into the 267.56 trim zone — treat 267.56 and 273.63 as partial scale-out levels, keep total single-name drawdown at ≤2% of portfolio value, cut to market weight on a daily close below 250.76, reduce to Underweight below 245.00, and never average down. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction goes with the operating evidence; size, entry geometry and add discipline go with the neutral analyst, whose corrections no one rebutted.

What the aggressive analyst won, unrefuted by either colleague: AMZN grew Q2 revenue +19.6% (accelerating from +16.6%), operating income +43.2% to $27.5B, operating margin +230bp to 13.7%, and TTM operating cash flow +33.2% to $161.4B — with inventory flat at $38.2B, marketing +2.5% against +19.6% revenue, and SBC down to 3.0% of revenue. Margins expanded while D&A was already running +31% y/y and capex was at peak intensity, which is operating leverage outrunning depreciation, and it is the hardest fact in the debate to explain away. On valuation, ~32x core EPS against ~29% core EPS growth is roughly a 1.1x PEG on an accelerating, margin-expanding franchise — a full multiple, not an indefensible one, and the conservative seat never produced a peer or historical anchor to make "priced for perfection" bite.

The conservative and neutral seats nonetheless won the risk composition of the trade, and I adopt it. First, negative free cash flow is not a sentiment issue: TTM FCF is −$11.6B because capex reached $173.0B (+60.7% y/y), Q2 capex was $54.2B (~$217B annualized) and 27% of revenue, and — decisively — capex rose sequentially from $44.2B, which punctures the bull's "if capex merely flattens, FCF inflects" conditional and is why the RM's own catalyst list puts Q3 capex first. Capex is ~2.3x TTM D&A, so the depreciation bill is still ahead. Second, leverage is a trajectory problem: gross debt +92% to $132.2B in six months, interest expense +155% to $1.314B and a flip to net interest expense, quick ratio 0.875, $650B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due inside a year. It is not a solvency problem — +$30.4B net cash ex-leases, net debt including leases under five months of operating cash flow, and Q2 interest at roughly 5% of $27.5B operating income — but the conservative is right that we underwrite the direction, not the snapshot. Third, earnings quality: $62.8B of H1 mark-up takes GAAP EPS to $5.75 versus ~$2.16 core, and the $122.3B non-marketable equity book is ~11.2% of assets, self-marked with no disclosed inputs. The aggressive's "latent strategic value" framing cannot be counted as a free option while the reversal risk is discounted; the correct treatment is the RM's — underwrite core EPS ex-mark-up, which still grew ~29%, and treat any downward mark as a size-reduction event, not a dip to buy.

The neutral analyst won the decisive exchange on mechanics, and that is what turns this into Overweight rather than Buy. The 253.50 entry sits *below* the 50-SMA at 253.95, so it is a support test, not a confirmed defensive line — the aggressive's 3:1 and 12:1 payoff math assumes a held level that price has not yet proven. The 250.76 daily-close stop is only $2.74 from entry against ATR of 6.69, i.e. under half an average daily range, and AMZN has gapped double digits in this record (July 31), so a close-only stop bounds intent, not realized loss: size, not the stop, is the protection. And the 267.75 add into the 267.56 rejection high is an internal contradiction with trimming at the same zone — I strike that tranche and replace it with a breakout-and-retest add requiring fundamental confirmation. Capping at 0.75–1.0x until AWS and Q3 are verified is the conservative's best point; the neutral's objection to it — that AWS segment data and Q3 guidance are simply absent from the record, so making them a precondition is paralysis — is answered by staging rather than by refusing the trade.

Where the bear genuinely scores, and where all three seats agree, is the tape: AMZN at $258.51 sits below the 10-EMA (259.14), the VWMA (259.78) and the 20-SMA, under a resistance stack at 259.14–262.20, against lower highs of 287.20 → 278.84 → 267.56, with MACD only 0.339 above zero, RSI 49.55, and a 9/4 fade from a 261.12 high. Volume drying up into the low (24.0M on 9/2 vs 90.8M on 8/3) and three sessions of histogram improvement are early stabilization, not demand. But the primary trend is intact — price 8.11% above a rising 200-SMA at 239.12, a widening golden-cross spread, and the 50-SMA held on closes since 7/30 — so this is an entry-timing constraint, not a thesis break. That asymmetry is precisely why I start near 0.30x rather than chasing and finish only on confirmation.

Prior lessons applied: repeated AMZN de-risking inside an intact rising 50/200 structure (07-22 to 07-30) cost 12–22% of five-day alpha, and the 08-27 staged Overweight produced +0.8% alpha — so I will not over-de-risk a franchise growing core earnings ~29%; but the 08-18 lesson, that a constructive rating parked at a bad entry geometry is the recurring failure mode, and the 08-28 GOOGL lesson, that a de-risk trigger ~2–3% from spot should be acted on rather than held through, both argue for small committed size at the support edge plus explicit triggers rather than a full clip at mid-range.

What would change the call. Up to a full Buy / 1.25x add: Q3 capex flattening sequentially below $54.2B, D&A growth no longer outrunning revenue, core EPS ex-mark-up still compounding ~25%+, gross debt and interest expense no longer compounding, contract liabilities inflecting off ~$24.9B, and disclosed AWS segment revenue and margin. Down to Hold/Underweight: a daily close below 250.76 (stand down, no averaging), a close below 245.00 (reduce), continued capex escalation with capex-to-revenue still rising, total debt pushing past ~$150B, marketing as a percentage of revenue rising while margins stall, any markdown in the $122.3B equity book, or a Q3 print where the operating-margin expansion reverses while capex stays above $50B/quarter. Reduce to market weight into the Q2 2027 mark-up anniversary rather than holding a full Overweight through a potential ~60% like-for-like GAAP EPS air pocket. Explicit gaps, stated and not papered over: AWS segment revenue and margin cannot be verified from this record, no Q3 guidance or capex plan was supplied, no sentiment/positioning or insider data is in the run, and there is no portfolio, holdings or cash context — so all sizing is expressed as a fraction of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation, and AMZN should be counted as one AI-capex-correlated position alongside any existing NVDA or hyperscaler exposure. The Riverside strike and the DOJ beef review carry no sizing weight on the evidence presented.

**Price Target**: 274.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months, re-scored on the Q3 print

REFLECTION:
The 5-day window shows −0.7% alpha against SPY, a mild negative that says little about a 3–6 month Overweight thesis and is far too short to score the Q3-print re-scoring plan; it mainly reflects the tape constraint the write-up already flagged. The entry-geometry caution was right in spirit — price sat below the 10-EMA, VWMA and 20-SMA under a 259.14–262.20 resistance stack, and the staged 0.30x at 252–254.50 did not get confirmation — while the capex, FCF and mark-up concerns remain untested by five days of price. Lesson: when the tape is the only live evidence, wait for the volume-confirmed close above 262.20 rather than starting the first tranche at a support test, since −0.7% alpha on 0.30x is the correct cost of doing so and costs nothing in thesis terms.

[2026-09-03 | AMZN | Underweight | -0.8% | +0.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: AMZN is **Underweight**, implemented as a staged partial reduction—not a full exit and not a short. Do not initiate a new AMZN long at **$258.90**. For a standard 100-unit AMZN allocation, reduce to roughly **70–75 units now**; if the caller is above standard weight or the account risk budget is already stretched, cut toward **50–65 units**. If the caller is already at or below the intended underweight, do not mechanically sell more—simply do not add. Use rallies into **$260.06–$263.00** to trim another **10–25 units** only if volume remains below **32.9M** and MACD remains below signal/negative. Treat **$264.00** as a closing-basis invalidation of the tactical bearish stance, not a tight intraday stop; size risk off a wider measure such as the 1.5-ATR distance near **$10.14** or the downside reference at **$250.47**. For the residual core, a daily close below **$250.47** on volume above **32.9M** should trigger a cut to **25–50 units**. Rebuild AMZN only on a confirmed reclaim of **$260.06** with volume above **32.9M**, positive MACD histogram and RSI above **55**, or after a stabilized washout into **$239–$250** with seller exhaustion. For mandates requiring AMZN exposure, protective puts or a collar around the reduced core are more appropriate than a naked short.

**Investment Thesis**: The direction is settled because all three risk seats and the trader support reducing AMZN; the real dispute is sizing and execution. The bear case wins enough for **Underweight**, but not enough for **Sell**. The technical evidence is clearly negative near term: AMZN at **$258.90** is below the 10 EMA at **$259.28**, below the VWMA at **$260.06**, and below the Bollinger mid at **$263.00**; MACD sits at **0.460** below its **1.814** signal with a histogram of **−1.354**; the Sep 3 bounce came on **26.89M** shares, only **0.82x** the roughly **32.85M** 20-day average; and RSI troughing at **46.33** is not a washout. The asymmetry is poor: upside to the **$260.06–$263.00** shelf is only about **$1–$4**, while a loss of **$250.47–$253.32** opens **$239–$240** and the 200 SMA, roughly **$19** lower.

The fundamental file supports trimming rather than adding. The Research Manager’s evidence shows AMZN H1 2026 FCF of **−$27.0B** versus **−$7.7B** in H1 2025, TTM capex of **$173.0B** at about **22%** of revenue, H1 capex up **72% y/y**, long-term debt rising from **$68.8B** to **$133.0B** in six months, Q2 interest expense doubling from **$516M** to **$1,314M**, and **$650.0B** of contractual obligations with **$78.1B** due within twelve months. Earnings quality is also a valuation risk: Q2 reported EPS of **$5.75** versus core EPS of roughly **$2.1**, H1 reported EPS of **$8.53** versus core roughly **$4.0**, more than **50%** of pre-tax income tied to non-cash equity marks, and the equity book expanding from **$16.2B** to **$122.3B** in six months. Those are enough to keep AMZN underweight at current price.

Why not **Sell**: the operating engine remains strong—Q2 revenue growth of about **19.6%**, operating income growth of **43.2%**, operating margin expansion of **226 bps**, and TTM operating cash flow of **$161.4B**. AMZN is also still above a rising 50 SMA near **$253.32** and a rising 200 SMA near **$238.99**, with the golden cross intact, debt-only net cash, and 20x+ interest coverage. That prevents a full-exit or short recommendation. Why not **Hold**: full weight at **$258.90** is poorly paid against the negative near-term asymmetry and unresolved cash-flow, debt, and earnings-quality risks.

On sizing, I side with the neutral analyst’s staged approach over the aggressive and conservative defaults. The aggressive analyst is right on the bearish tape and asymmetry but too quick to lean toward **50 units** by default: the **$264.00** stop is only about **$5.10 / 2.0%** above spot against an ATR of **$6.758**, so it sits inside one normal day’s range and cannot be used as a precise sizing anchor, especially with no holdings or cash context. The conservative analyst is right to frame this as risk control and to use **$264.00** as a closing-basis invalidation rather than an intraday hair trigger, but a default cut to **50–60 units** without portfolio context is arbitrary. The neutral analyst best balances the evidence: AMZN formed a short-term higher low at **$256.00**, the MACD histogram contracted from **−1.585** to **−1.354**, and the primary trend has not broken—so start at **70–75 units**, not 50, while preserving clear triggers to cut to **50–65** if the caller is above standard weight, risk budget is stretched, AMZN fails into **$260.06–$263.00** on weak volume, or closes below **$250.47** on volume above **32.9M**.

What would change the call: upgrade toward **Hold/Overweight** on a confirmed reclaim of **$260.06** with volume above **32.9M**, positive MACD histogram and RSI above **55**; or after a stabilized washout into **$239–$250** with clear seller exhaustion and improving momentum; or on fundamental evidence of capex deceleration, FCF inflection, disclosure splitting customer-backed versus unconditional obligations, normalized cash tax rate, and no markdown in the **$122.3B** equity-mark book. Downgrade toward **Sell** on a daily close below **$250.47** on volume above **32.9M** that fails to reclaim **$253.32**, or on further deterioration in debt, FCF, or the equity-mark book. Data gaps remain material: no portfolio, holdings, or cash context was provided; AMZN AWS segment detail is not supplied in the debate; the news/sentiment sample is incomplete; and no external tools were used to verify the fundamental figures beyond the supplied materials.

REFLECTION:
The 5-day alpha of +0.3% (raw −0.8% vs SPY) does not support the Underweight directional call, since AMZN modestly outperformed the benchmark, though five days is too short to judge the thesis. This undercuts the near-term technical/asymmetry leg—below the 10 EMA/VWMA/Bollinger mid with only $1–$4 upside versus ~$19 downside—while leaving the FCF/debt/earnings-quality case untested and mildly supporting the “not Sell” caution because no $250.47 breakdown occurred. Lesson: predefine a horizon-matched check, such as 20–60 day relative performance vs SPY, before letting a 5-day alpha adjust a staged Underweight.

[2026-09-02 | AMZN | Underweight | -1.2% | -0.3% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN: trim existing exposure by roughly one-third to one-half, taking a standard allocation to ~50–60%, and execute at least three-quarters of that reduction at market near $254.98 rather than posting sell limits above spot — the last two windows showed AMZN does not owe us a bounce, and the bull's own add-triggers ($260.4–$263.66 on >40M shares) sit above the current price. Do not initiate or add at $254.98, and do not short a name with $176.1B of liquid assets and a rising 50/200-day structure. Carry the residual with a hard stop on a daily close below $250.64 (breach opens $238.87, the 200-day inside the unfilled July gap, −6.3%), sized so that gap is a bad quarter, not a portfolio event. Rebuild only on a reclaim of $260.4–$263.66 on >40M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive and RSI back above 55 — half the trimmed amount at confirmation, the rest on a higher low above $260 — and only with at least one fundamental gate cleared. Horizon 3–6 months, re-scored on the late-October Q3 print.

**Investment Thesis**: All three seats converged on reducing AMZN; they split only on size and re-entry mechanics, so the work here is deciding which critique of execution is strongest — and on that the conservative and neutral seats beat the aggressive seat's confidence, while the aggressive seat beats the conservative seat's rigidity.

**What decides the direction.** The bull's operating case is not contested and I credit it fully: Q2 2026 revenue $200.6B (+19.6%), operating income $27.5B (+43.2%), margin 13.7% (+226 bps), H1 operating income $51.3B (+36.6%), higher lows intact at $198.79 → $225.55 → $226.16 → $251.93, price $254.98 above a rising 50-day ($252.83) and 6.7% above a rising 200-day ($238.87). That is why this is not a Sell. What decides the rating is that the price no longer pays for the risk being carried. Three items did it.
